Generate the intervention data for a population

Source: R/interventions.R
generate_intervention_data.Rd

Determines which locations have an intervention deployed, and the resulting per-location efficacy for each setting with an active intervention. This is kept separate from generate_population_data() so that the same population can be reused with different interventions.

It seeds the random number generators itself, so its result does not depend on earlier random draws, and it is the intervention data that run_simulation() uses. When parameters_list$seed is the seed the population was built with, it continues the population's random stream, as if the population and the intervention were drawn in one go. Otherwise it starts a new stream from parameters_list$seed.

It errors if population_data was built from different values of the population parameters than parameters_list (see generate_population_data()).

Usage

generate_intervention_data(parameters_list, population_data)

Arguments

parameters_list

A list of model parameters as generated using get_parameters()

population_data

A list representing the population, containing at least the setting_sizes, <setting>_specific_ach and <setting>_specific_riskiness entries, as generated by generate_population_data()

Value

A list with three elements:

switches

The coverage switches, as returned by generate_intervention_switches().

efficacy

A named list containing, for each setting with an active intervention, the per-location efficacy as returned by calculate_efficacy_from_ach().

timestep

A named list containing, for each setting with an active intervention, its intervention_<setting>_timestep: efficacy is applied at the timesteps after it.

A joint intervention counts as active in the workplace, school and leisure settings, with the joint intervention list and timestep.

See also
